text: A farmer picked {A} apples in the morning and {B} more in the afternoon, then sold {C} apples at the market. He worked for {D1} hours that day. How many apples does he have left?
note: Add two harvests then subtract sold apples.

text: Maria had {A} stickers and got {B} more from a friend, then gave away {C} stickers to her sister. How many stickers does she have now?
note: Add gains then subtract given-away stickers.

text: A bakery made {A} loaves of bread and {B} more later in the day, then donated {C} loaves to a shelter. How many loaves are left?
note: Add two batches then subtract donated loaves.

text: A train had {A} passengers, picked up {B} more at the next stop, then {C} passengers got off. How many passengers remain on the train?
note: Add boarding passengers then subtract those leaving.

text: Sam scored {A} points in a game and {B} points in another game, then lost {C} points for a penalty. What is his final score?
note: Add two game scores then subtract a penalty.

text: A library received {A} new books and {B} donated books, then removed {C} damaged books from the shelf. How many books are on the shelf now?
note: Add two intakes then subtract damaged books.

text: Each basket has {A} red marbles and {B} blue marbles, and there are {C} baskets. The baskets were bought for {D1} dollars each. How many marbles are there in total?
note: Add colors per basket then multiply by basket count.

text: A box holds {A} pencils and {B} pens, and a store has {C} such boxes. How many items are there in all the boxes together?
note: Add items per box then multiply by box count.

text: Each classroom has {A} boys and {B} girls, and the school has {C} classrooms. How many students are there in the whole school?
note: Add students per room then multiply by rooms.

text: A recipe uses {A} cups of flour and {B} cups of sugar, and a baker makes {C} batches of the recipe. How many cups of flour and sugar are used in total?
note: Add cups per batch then multiply by batches.

text: Each shelf holds {A} novels and {B} comics, and the store has {C} shelves. How many books are there altogether?
note: Add books per shelf then multiply by shelves.

text: A farm keeps {A} hens and {B} ducks in each coop, and there are {C} coops on the farm. How many birds are there in total?
note: Add birds per coop then multiply by coops.

text: A parking lot had {A} cars, then {B} cars left, and later {C} more cars arrived. The lot has {D1} lights installed. How many cars are in the lot now?
note: Subtract cars that left then add new arrivals.

text: Jake had {A} marbles, lost {B} of them in a game, then won {C} more in the next round. How many marbles does he have now?
note: Subtract lost marbles then add winnings.

text: A theater had {A} seats filled, {B} people left during intermission, and then {C} new people came in. How many seats are filled now?
note: Subtract people who left then add new arrivals.

text: A warehouse stored {A} boxes, shipped out {B} boxes, and then received {C} new boxes from a supplier. How many boxes are in the warehouse now?
note: Subtract shipped boxes then add a new delivery.

text: A team had {A} players, {B} got injured and sat out, then {C} substitutes joined the game. How many players are active now?
note: Subtract injured players then add substitutes.

text: A pond had {A} fish, {B} were caught by fishermen, and then {C} more fish were added. How many fish are in the pond now?
note: Subtract caught fish then add new fish.

text: A store sells {A} boxes of cookies with {B} cookies in each box, plus {C} loose cookies. The store has {D1} employees today. How many cookies are there in total?
note: Multiply boxed cookies then add loose ones.

text: A bus company runs {A} buses with {B} seats each, and there are also {C} standing passengers on the route. How many people can the buses carry in total?
note: Multiply seats by buses then add standing riders.

text: A farmer plants {A} rows with {B} trees in each row, plus {C} extra trees near the fence. How many trees are there in total?
note: Multiply rows by trees then add extras.

text: A worker earns {A} dollars an hour for {B} hours, plus a {C} dollar bonus. How much money does the worker have in total?
note: Multiply wage by hours then add a bonus.

text: A garden has {A} beds with {B} flowers in each bed, plus {C} flowers in pots on the porch. How many flowers are there altogether?
note: Multiply beds by flowers then add potted ones.

text: A printer makes {A} copies of a flyer {B} times a day, plus {C} extra copies for the office. How many flyers are printed in total?
note: Multiply copies by runs then add extras.

text: A vendor sells {A} bags of oranges with {B} oranges in each bag, then {C} oranges spoil and are thrown out. The vendor traveled {D1} miles to the market. How many oranges are left?
note: Multiply bags by oranges then subtract spoiled ones.

text: A school orders {A} boxes of chairs with {B} chairs in each box, but {C} chairs arrive broken. How many usable chairs are there?
note: Multiply boxes by chairs then subtract broken ones.

text: A farmer harvests {A} crates of corn with {B} ears in each crate, then sells {C} ears at the market. How many ears of corn are left?
note: Multiply crates by ears then subtract sold ears.

text: A factory packs {A} trucks with {B} boxes each, but {C} boxes fall off during loading. How many boxes make it to the destination?
note: Multiply trucks by boxes then subtract lost boxes.

text: A coach buys {A} packs of jerseys with {B} jerseys in each pack, then returns {C} jerseys that don't fit. How many jerseys are kept?
note: Multiply packs by jerseys then subtract returns.

text: A baker bakes {A} trays of muffins with {B} muffins on each tray, then {C} muffins burn and are thrown away. How many muffins are good?
note: Multiply trays by muffins then subtract burnt ones.

text: A charity splits {A} dollars evenly among {B} families, and then gives each family an extra {C} dollars. The charity event lasted {D1} hours. How many dollars does each family get?
note: Divide money evenly then add an extra amount.

text: A teacher divides {A} pencils evenly among {B} students, then hands out {C} more pencils to each student. How many pencils does each student have now?
note: Divide pencils evenly then add more per student.

text: A baker splits {A} cookies evenly onto {B} plates, then adds {C} more cookies to each plate. How many cookies are on each plate now?
note: Divide cookies evenly then add more per plate.

text: A coach divides {A} balls evenly among {B} teams, then buys each team {C} more balls. How many balls does each team have now?
note: Divide balls evenly then add more per team.

text: A farmer splits {A} eggs evenly into {B} cartons, then adds {C} more eggs to each carton. How many eggs are in each carton now?
note: Divide eggs evenly then add more per carton.

text: A store has {A} shelves with {B} cans on each shelf, and the cans are repacked evenly into boxes of {C}. How many boxes are needed?
note: Multiply shelves by cans then divide into boxes.

text: A school has {A} classes with {B} students in each class, and the students are split evenly into groups of {C}. How many groups are there?
note: Multiply classes by students then divide into groups.

text: A factory makes {A} batches of {B} widgets each, and the widgets are packed evenly into crates of {C}. How many crates are filled?
note: Multiply batches by widgets then divide into crates.

text: A farm harvests {A} baskets with {B} apples in each basket, and the apples are bagged evenly with {C} apples in each bag. How many bags are filled?
note: Multiply baskets by apples then divide into bags.

text: A theater sells {A} rows of {B} tickets each, and the tickets are bundled evenly into sets of {C}. How many sets are there?
note: Multiply rows by tickets then divide into sets.

text: What is the difference between {A} and {B}?

text: How far apart are {A} and {B} on a number line?
note: Distance phrasing hides an absolute difference.

text: By how much do {A} and {B} differ?
note: Short difference question with no fixed order.

text: Ana is {A} years old and her brother is {B} years old. What is the age gap between them?
note: Age gap story hiding an absolute difference.

text: A runner finished in {A} seconds and another runner finished in {B} seconds. What is the gap between their times?
note: Race times story hiding an absolute difference.

text: What is {A} plus {B} plus {C}?
note: Three-term sum, not a two-step problem.

text: Add {A}, {B} and {C} together.
note: Plain instruction to sum three numbers.

text: A shopper buys items priced at {A} dollars, {B} dollars and {C} dollars. What is the sum of these prices?
note: Shopping story wrapping a three-term sum.

text: Find the total of {A}, {B} and {C}.
note: Direct request for a three-term total.

text: A runner covers {A} miles, then {B} miles, then {C} miles on a trail. What is the combined distance?
note: Trail distances that just add straight through.

text: What is {A} minus {B} minus {C}?
note: Repeated subtraction, a single chained operation.

text: A wallet has {A} dollars. Subtract {B} dollars, then subtract {C} dollars. What is left?

text: Multiply {A} by {B} and then by {C}.
note: Repeated multiplication, a single chained operation.

text: What do you get if you multiply {A}, {B} and {C} together?
note: Three-way product phrased as one question.

text: Start with {A}. Add {B} to it, and then add {C}. What is the result?
